question: Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 regulates the use of food additives, including phosphoric acid and phosphates designated by E numbers 338-452. These substances are used in certain meat products for technological reasons, including to improve the properties of the products.

At the same time, the use of phosphates may raise questions regarding consumers’ cumulative exposure and the transparency of information on product composition. It is also important to note that the permitted levels of use for individual additives depend on the food category, and their interpretation requires consideration of the relevant specific provisions. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission envisage a review of the permitted uses and levels of phosphates E 338-452 in meat products in the light of current data on total consumer exposure to phosphates from various sources?
Does the Commission have inspection results indicating that the permitted levels of phosphates in meat products placed on the EU market have been exceeded?
Is the Commission considering additional labelling requirements to enable consumers to more easily identify the presence of phosphates in processed meat products?
